sections.title: CONCEPT 1: BM25 vs Dense Retrieval — Strengths and Weaknesses
sections.body:
### ① Concept Explanation

BM25 is a term-based probabilistic model that scores documents using exact token overlap, IDF weighting, and length normalisation. Dense retrieval (BERT-based bi-encoders) maps queries and documents to fixed-dimensional continuous vectors and scores by cosine or dot product similarity. BM25 has zero training data requirement, perfect recall for exact-match queries, and full interpretability — every score can be explained by term frequency and IDF. Dense retrieval handles vocabulary mismatch and paraphrase, but requires large annotated datasets and GPU inference. The **BEIR benchmark** (Thakur et al., 2021) showed that BM25 outperforms many zero-shot dense models on out-of-domain tasks, making it a surprisingly strong baseline.

$$\text{BM25}: S(q,d) = \sum_{t \in q} \text{IDF}(t) \cdot \frac{f(t,d)(k_1+1)}{f(t,d) + k_1(1-b+b\frac{|d|}{\text{avgdl}})}$$

$$\text{Dense}: S(q,d) = \frac{E_q \cdot E_d}{||E_q|| \cdot ||E_d||}$$

### ② 10 Conceptual Questions & Answers

**Q1. What are BM25's strengths and weaknesses vs dense retrieval?**

```python
# STRENGTHS AND WEAKNESSES — HEAD-TO-HEAD COMPARISON

comparison = {
    "BM25": {
        "strengths": [
            "Zero training data required — works out of the box",
            "Perfect exact-match recall — 'COVID-19' always matches 'COVID-19'",
            "Fully interpretable — explain any score from term weights",
            "Lightning fast — 10–50ms for 100M docs in Elasticsearch",
            "Low infrastructure cost — no GPU needed",
            "No vocabulary mismatch for well-chosen query terms",
            "Robust to domain shift — same model for medical/legal/code",
            "Proven at scale — Elasticsearch powers >40% of global search",
        ],
        "weaknesses": [
            "Vocabulary mismatch — 'heart attack' ≠ 'myocardial infarction'",
            "No semantic understanding — 'not great' treated as 'great'",
            "No query expansion — misses synonyms unless added manually",
            "No personalisation — same result for all users, same query",
            "Sensitive to tokenisation — stemming errors affect results",
            "IDF drift — corpus growth changes term weights over time",
        ],
    },
    "Dense (Bi-encoder)": {
        "strengths": [
            "Semantic matching — 'buy', 'purchase', 'acquire' are similar",
            "Cross-lingual — multilingual models match across languages",
            "Paraphrase recall — finds semantically equivalent passages",
            "Personalisation — fine-tune on user signals (click logs)",
            "Zero query expansion needed — model handles it implicitly",
        ],
        "weaknesses": [
            "Requires large annotated datasets (MS-MARCO: 500K pairs)",
            "Expensive inference — GPU needed for low latency at scale",
            "Domain shift — BERT-base trained on news fails on legal text",
            "Catastrophic on exact-match — 'SKU-ABC-123' may not be in vocab",
            "Black box — hard to debug 'why was X retrieved?'",
            "ANN index drift — adding docs requires re-indexing FAISS",
            "Sensitive to fine-tuning quality — bad negatives → poor model",
        ],
    }
}

def print_comparison():
    for system, data in comparison.items():
        print(f"\n{'='*50}")
        print(f"  {system}")
        print(f"{'='*50}")
        print("  STRENGTHS:")
        for s in data["strengths"]:
            print(f"    ✓ {s}")
        print("  WEAKNESSES:")
        for w in data["weaknesses"]:
            print(f"    ✗ {w}")

print_comparison()
```

**Q2. What is the BEIR benchmark and what does it show?**

```python
# BEIR: Benchmarking Information Retrieval out-of-the-box
# 18 diverse IR tasks: biomedical, financial, scientific, legal, ...
# Key finding: BM25 often BEATS zero-shot dense models

beir_results = {
    # NDCG@10 scores on BEIR tasks (approximate from paper)
    "Task":             ["NQ",   "MS-MARCO", "TREC-COVID", "BioASQ", "NFCorpus", "Robust04"],
    "BM25":             [0.329,    0.228,        0.656,      0.465,     0.325,       0.408],
    "DPR (zero-shot)":  [0.474,    0.184,        0.332,      0.127,     0.181,       0.163],
    "ANCE (zero-shot)": [0.456,    0.338,        0.654,      0.155,     0.237,       0.222],
    "BM25+CE rerank":   [0.595,    0.395,        0.796,      0.512,     0.388,       0.507],
}

# Key insight:
# DPR (trained on NQ) degrades catastrophically on TREC-COVID (0.332 vs BM25's 0.656)
# ANCE (trained on MS-MARCO) loses to BM25 on BioASQ, NFCorpus, Robust04
# BM25 is a strong zero-shot baseline for out-of-domain tasks
# BM25 + cross-encoder reranker is near-optimal for most tasks

print("BEIR NDCG@10 comparison:")
print(f"{'Task':<15} {'BM25':>6} {'DPR':>6} {'ANCE':>6} {'BM25+CE':>8}")
for i, task in enumerate(beir_results["Task"]):
    print(f"{task:<15} "
          f"{beir_results['BM25'][i]:>6.3f} "
          f"{beir_results['DPR (zero-shot)'][i]:>6.3f} "
          f"{beir_results['ANCE (zero-shot)'][i]:>6.3f} "
          f"{beir_results['BM25+CE rerank'][i]:>8.3f}")
```

**Q3. When should you choose BM25 over dense retrieval?**

```python
def retrieval_strategy_decision(use_case: dict) -> str:
    """
    Decision framework: BM25 vs Dense vs Hybrid.
    
    Inputs:
    - domain:              "general" | "technical" | "medical" | "legal" | "ecommerce"
    - query_type:          "keyword" | "semantic" | "mixed"
    - training_data_avail: True | False
    - latency_budget_ms:   int
    - interpretability:    "required" | "preferred" | "not_needed"
    - exact_match_critical: True | False  (SKUs, codes, citations)
    """
    score_bm25   = 0
    score_dense  = 0
    score_hybrid = 0
    
    if use_case["exact_match_critical"]:
        score_bm25   += 3
        score_hybrid += 2
    
    if use_case["query_type"] == "keyword":
        score_bm25   += 2
    elif use_case["query_type"] == "semantic":
        score_dense  += 3
        score_hybrid += 2
    else:  # mixed
        score_hybrid += 3
    
    if not use_case["training_data_avail"]:
        score_bm25 += 3
        score_dense -= 2  # dense needs training data
    
    if use_case["latency_budget_ms"] < 50:
        score_bm25  += 2
        score_dense -= 1  # GPU inference overhead
    
    if use_case["interpretability"] == "required":
        score_bm25   += 3
        score_dense  -= 2  # black box
        score_hybrid += 0  # hybrid adds complexity
    
    if use_case["domain"] in ["medical", "legal"]:
        score_bm25   += 1  # exact terminology
        score_hybrid += 1  # benefit from semantic too
    
    scores = {"BM25": score_bm25, "Dense": score_dense, "Hybrid": score_hybrid}
    winner = max(scores, key=scores.get)
    
    print(f"Scores: {scores}")
    print(f"→ Recommended: {winner}")
    return winner

# Examples
decision1 = retrieval_strategy_decision({
    "domain": "ecommerce", "query_type": "mixed",
    "training_data_avail": True, "latency_budget_ms": 100,
    "interpretability": "preferred", "exact_match_critical": True,
})  # → Hybrid

decision2 = retrieval_strategy_decision({
    "domain": "legal", "query_type": "keyword",
    "training_data_avail": False, "latency_budget_ms": 30,
    "interpretability": "required", "exact_match_critical": True,
})  # → BM25
```

**Q4. What is the vocabulary mismatch problem and how does each approach handle it?**

```python
from rank_bm25 import BM25Okapi
from langchain_community.retrievers import BM25Retriever
from langchain_core.documents import Document

def demonstrate_vocabulary_mismatch():
    """
    Vocabulary mismatch: query and document use different words for same concept.
    BM25: FAILS. Dense: SUCCEEDS. Hybrid: best of both.
    """
    # Medical synonyms
    corpus = [
        "The patient suffered a myocardial infarction requiring immediate intervention.",
        "The patient complained of chest pain radiating to the left arm.",
        "The ECG showed ST-segment elevation consistent with STEMI.",
    ]
    
    bm25 = BM25Okapi([doc.split() for doc in corpus])
    
    # Query uses "heart attack" but corpus uses "myocardial infarction"
    query = "heart attack treatment"
    scores = bm25.get_scores(query.split())
    
    print("BM25 scores for 'heart attack treatment':")
    for doc, score in zip(corpus, scores):
        print(f"  Score {score:.3f}: {doc[:60]}...")
    
    # BM25 gives score ~0 for doc1 (no token overlap with "heart attack")
    # Dense retrieval would score doc1 HIGHEST (semantic similarity)
    
    print("\nBM25 vocabulary mismatch demonstrated: doc 1 (most relevant) scores ~0")
    print("Fix options:")
    print("  1. Manual synonym dict: 'heart attack' → 'myocardial infarction OR MI'")
    print("  2. SPLADE implicit expansion")
    print("  3. Hybrid: dense retrieval rescues doc 1")
    print("  4. WordNet expansion")
    
    # Fix: query expansion
    expansion_dict = {
        "heart attack": ["myocardial infarction", "MI", "cardiac arrest", "STEMI"],
    }
    expanded_query = "heart attack myocardial infarction MI cardiac arrest treatment"
    scores_expanded = bm25.get_scores(expanded_query.split())
    
    print("\nBM25 scores after query expansion:")
    for doc, score in zip(corpus, scores_expanded):
        print(f"  Score {score:.3f}: {doc[:60]}...")

demonstrate_vocabulary_mismatch()
```

**Q5. What is the difference between bi-encoder and cross-encoder, and where does BM25 fit?**

```python
# Three-stage ranking pipeline:
# Stage 1: BM25 (fast, high recall) → top 100-1000 candidates
# Stage 2: Bi-encoder (GPU, fast ANN) → top 50-100 candidates  
# Stage 3: Cross-encoder (GPU, slow but accurate) → top 10-20 final

def three_stage_pipeline(query: str,
                           bm25_retriever,
                           bi_encoder_model,
                           cross_encoder_model,
                           docs: list[Document],
                           k_bm25: int = 100,
                           k_bi: int = 20,
                           k_final: int = 5) -> list[Document]:
    """
    Full three-stage ranking pipeline.
    
    BM25:  O(posting_list_size) — ~10ms
    ANN:   O(log n) — ~20ms
    CE:    O(k_bi) — ~50ms (k_bi × inference)
    Total: ~80ms
    """
    from sentence_transformers import CrossEncoder
    
    # Stage 1: BM25 — coarse filtering
    bm25_results = bm25_retriever.invoke(query)[:k_bm25]
    print(f"Stage 1 (BM25):        {len(bm25_results)} candidates")
    
    # Stage 2: Bi-encoder — dense re-ranking
    # query_emb  = bi_encoder_model.encode(query)
    # doc_embs   = bi_encoder_model.encode([d.page_content for d in bm25_results])
    # sim_scores = np.dot(doc_embs, query_emb)
    # bi_results = [bm25_results[i] for i in np.argsort(-sim_scores)[:k_bi]]
    bi_results = bm25_results[:k_bi]  # demo
    print(f"Stage 2 (Bi-encoder):  {len(bi_results)} candidates")
    
    # Stage 3: Cross-encoder — precise re-ranking
    # pairs  = [(query, doc.page_content) for doc in bi_results]
    # scores = cross_encoder_model.predict(pairs)
    # final  = [bi_results[i] for i in np.argsort(-scores)[:k_final]]
    final = bi_results[:k_final]  # demo
    print(f"Stage 3 (Cross-enc):   {len(final)} final results")
    
    return final
```

**Q9. How does negation handling differ between BM25 and dense retrieval?**

**A:** BM25 has **no semantic negation awareness** — "not good" and "good" share the token "good" and receive similar scores. Dense retrieval models also struggle but less so: "not good" has a different embedding than "good" because BERT processes context. The best fix for BM25 is to use boolean query syntax (must/must_not in Elasticsearch). For dense models, the negation error rate is lower but still measurable — verified by the "NLI as retrieval" experiments showing BM25 often outperforms dense on hypothesis retrieval.

**Q10. What is the industry consensus on BM25 vs neural?**

**A:** The practical industry conclusion (2024) is: **use hybrid by default**. BM25 handles exact match and is the safety net; dense retrieval handles semantic queries. The BEIR finding that zero-shot BM25 beats zero-shot dense on many tasks has slowed the pure-dense adoption. For most production systems: BM25 at retrieval → bi-encoder re-rank → cross-encoder final ranking. SPLADE has emerged as a strong middle ground — trained sparse vectors that use an inverted index (no GPU at query time) but understand semantics better than BM25.

### ③ 10 Scenario-Based Questions & Answers

**S1. 💼 Stakeholder says "We have BERT, why use BM25 at all?"**

```python
# The "BM25 is old tech, we have neural" argument
# Counter-argument: BEIR benchmark + latency + cost + interpretability

def argue_for_hybrid_system(stakeholder_objection: str) -> str:
    responses = {
        "BM25 is old": """
BM25 is not old — it is proven. BERT-based dense retrieval:
1. Requires 10K–100K labeled training pairs per domain.
2. Degrades on exact-match queries (SKUs, error codes, citations).
3. Needs GPU at query time → 5–10× inference cost.
4. BEIR shows BM25 beats zero-shot dense on 9 of 18 tasks.

Hybrid BM25 + dense outperforms either alone. BM25 is not a legacy — 
it is a critical component of the hybrid stack.
        """,
        "dense handles everything": """
Dense retrieval has systematic failures:
- 'COVID-19' vs 'coronavirus' — dense handles well
- 'model.fit(X_train, y_train)' — BM25 handles, dense may not
- 'SEC filing 10-K 2023' — BM25 exact match wins
- 'product id A-123-XL' — BM25 wins

Running BM25 in parallel costs almost nothing (CPU-only) and 
prevents catastrophic failures on exact-match queries.
        """,
    }
    return responses.get(stakeholder_objection, "Evaluate on your specific domain with BEIR.")

def run_domain_specific_beir_eval(domain_corpus: list[dict],
                                   domain_queries: list[dict],
                                   bm25_retriever, dense_retriever) -> dict:
    """
    Run mini-BEIR evaluation on your domain to justify hybrid.
    Present results to stakeholder: data beats opinion.
    """
    bm25_ndcg  = []
    dense_ndcg = []
    
    for qa in domain_queries:
        query   = qa["question"]
        rel_set = set(qa["relevant_doc_ids"])
        
        bm25_hits   = bm25_retriever.invoke(query)
        dense_hits  = dense_retriever.invoke(query)
        
        bm25_ids  = [d.metadata["id"] for d in bm25_hits[:10]]
        dense_ids = [d.metadata["id"] for d in dense_hits[:10]]
        
        rel_graded = {d: 1 for d in rel_set}
        bm25_ndcg.append( ndcg_at_k(bm25_ids,  rel_graded, k=10))
        dense_ndcg.append(ndcg_at_k(dense_ids, rel_graded, k=10))
    
    result = {
        "BM25 NDCG@10":  float(np.mean(bm25_ndcg)),
        "Dense NDCG@10": float(np.mean(dense_ndcg)),
        "Winner":        "BM25" if np.mean(bm25_ndcg) > np.mean(dense_ndcg) else "Dense",
    }
    print("Domain-specific evaluation:")
    for k, v in result.items():
        print(f"  {k}: {v}")
    return result

import numpy as np

def ndcg_at_k(retrieved, relevance, k):
    gains = [relevance.get(d, 0) for d in retrieved[:k]]
    ideal = sorted(relevance.values(), reverse=True)[:k]
    def dcg(s): return sum((2**r-1)/np.log2(i+2) for i,r in enumerate(s))
    idcg = dcg(ideal)
    return dcg(gains) / idcg if idcg > 0 else 0.0
```

**S2. 💥 Zero-shot dense retrieval underperforms BM25 on internal docs.**

```python
# Scenario: company deploys FAISS + sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM
# Retrieval quality worse than BM25 on internal documentation
# Root cause: model trained on web data, not domain-specific text

def diagnose_dense_underperformance(bm25_retriever, dense_retriever,
                                    eval_queries: list[dict]) -> dict:
    """
    Systematic diagnosis of dense underperformance.
    """
    failure_categories = {
        "exact_match": [],
        "domain_jargon": [],
        "semantic": [],
    }
    
    for qa in eval_queries:
        query   = qa["question"]
        rel_ids = set(qa["relevant_doc_ids"])
        
        bm25_results  = bm25_retriever.invoke(query)[:10]
        dense_results = dense_retriever.invoke(query)[:10]
        
        bm25_recall   = len({d.metadata["id"] for d in bm25_results} & rel_ids) / max(len(rel_ids), 1)
        dense_recall  = len({d.metadata["id"] for d in dense_results} & rel_ids) / max(len(rel_ids), 1)
        
        if bm25_recall > dense_recall + 0.2:
            # BM25 significantly better — why?
            # Heuristic classification
            if any(char.isdigit() for char in query):
                failure_categories["exact_match"].append(query)
            elif len(set(query.split()) - {"the","is","a","of","in","for"}) < 3:
                failure_categories["domain_jargon"].append(query)
    
    fixes = {
        "exact_match":   "→ Use BM25 for exact-match, add to hybrid",
        "domain_jargon": "→ Fine-tune dense model on domain data (10K+ pairs)",
        "semantic":      "→ Dense should win here — check tokeniser / model",
    }
    
    print("Dense failure diagnosis:")
    for cat, queries in failure_categories.items():
        print(f"  {cat} ({len(queries)} failures): {fixes[cat]}")
    
    return failure_categories
```

**S3. ⚖️ Legal citation retrieval — BM25 wins decisively.**

```python
# Legal use case: find relevant case citations
# Queries like: "Smith v. Jones, 2019 USCA 145"
# Dense: embeds to "legal case involving Smith" → wrong cases
# BM25: exact case name match → correct citation

from rank_bm25 import BM25Okapi

def legal_citation_retrieval():
    """Demonstrate BM25 superiority for exact citation matching."""
    
    legal_corpus = [
        "Smith v. Jones 2019 USCA 145 - contract breach negligence standard",
        "Johnson v. State 2018 USCA 099 - criminal procedure Miranda rights",
        "Tech Corp v. Patent LLC 2021 CAFC 222 - software patent obviousness",
        "Employee v. Employer 2020 NLRB 031 - wrongful termination at-will",
    ]
    
    bm25 = BM25Okapi([doc.split() for doc in legal_corpus])
    
    # Exact citation query
    query = "Smith v. Jones 2019 USCA"
    scores = bm25.get_scores(query.split())
    
    print("Legal citation BM25 scores:")
    for doc, score in sorted(zip(legal_corpus, scores), key=lambda x: -x[1]):
        print(f"  {score:.3f}: {doc}")
    
    # Dense would embed "Smith v. Jones" semantically
    # and might return "Employee v. Employer" (also an employer-employee case)
    # BM25 correctly ranks "Smith v. Jones 2019 USCA 145" first

    # Hybrid: use BM25 score as hard gate for citations
    def citation_aware_retrieval(query: str, corpus: list[str], bm25,
                                  top_k: int = 5) -> list[str]:
        """
        Use citation detection to route to BM25 or dense.
        """
        import re
        citation_pattern = r'\b\d{4}\b|\bv\.\s|USCA|CAFC|NLRB'
        is_citation_query = bool(re.search(citation_pattern, query, re.I))
        
        if is_citation_query:
            scores = bm25.get_scores(query.split())
            ranked = sorted(range(len(corpus)), key=lambda i: -scores[i])[:top_k]
            return [corpus[i] for i in ranked]
        else:
            # Fall through to dense retrieval
            return []  # demo
    
    return citation_aware_retrieval(query, legal_corpus, bm25)

result = legal_citation_retrieval()
```

**S5. 🔬 Domain adaptation: fine-tune dense model to match BM25 on medical text.**

```python
# SCENARIO: BM25 outperforms BERT on medical QA
# SOLUTION: domain-adaptive pre-training + contrastive fine-tuning

def generate_training_pairs_from_bm25(queries: list[str],
                                       corpus: list[dict],
                                       bm25_retriever,
                                       dense_retriever,
                                       top_k: int = 100) -> list[dict]:
    """
    Generate hard negatives for dense model training using BM25.
    
    Strategy: BM25 top-K docs that are NOT relevant = hard negatives.
    This teaches dense model the exact-match patterns BM25 excels at.
    """
    training_pairs = []
    
    for query in queries:
        bm25_results  = bm25_retriever.invoke(query)[:top_k]
        dense_results = dense_retriever.invoke(query)[:top_k]
        
        # Use first BM25 result as positive (if high score)
        positive = bm25_results[0] if bm25_results else None
        
        # Use low-ranked BM25 results as hard negatives (retrieved but not relevant)
        hard_negatives = [d for d in bm25_results[50:70]]  # ranks 51-70 are good hard negatives
        
        if positive and hard_negatives:
            training_pairs.append({
                "query":           query,
                "positive":        positive.page_content,
                "hard_negatives":  [d.page_content for d in hard_negatives[:5]],
            })
    
    print(f"Generated {len(training_pairs)} training pairs")
    print("Fine-tune with sentence-transformers MultipleNegativesRankingLoss")
    return training_pairs
```

**S7. 📱 Mobile / edge deployment — BM25 wins for offline.**

```python
# Edge deployment: smartphone app, offline search
# Dense model: 22M–110M params, 80MB–440MB, needs GPU for speed
# BM25: pure Python, 2KB per document, no GPU

def build_lightweight_bm25_index(corpus: list[dict],
                                   max_docs: int = 10_000) -> dict:
    """
    Lightweight BM25 for edge/mobile deployment.
    Subset corpus to device capacity.
    """
    from rank_bm25 import BM25Okapi
    import pickle
    
    # Limit corpus for mobile
    device_corpus = corpus[:max_docs]
    tokenized     = [doc["content"].lower().split() for doc in device_corpus]
    bm25          = BM25Okapi(tokenized)
    
    # Serialise for mobile
    import io
    buffer = io.BytesIO()
    pickle.dump({"bm25": bm25, "docs": device_corpus}, buffer)
    size_mb = buffer.tell() / 1024**2
    
    print(f"BM25 index for {max_docs:,} docs: {size_mb:.1f} MB")
    print(f"Dense model (MiniLM):              ~80 MB (without runtime)")
    print(f"→ BM25 wins for edge deployment: smaller, no GPU, interpretable")
    
    return {"size_mb": size_mb, "n_docs": max_docs}
```

```python
def code_search_comparison():

    for doc, score in sorted(zip(code_corpus, scores), key=lambda x: -x[1]):
        print(f"  {score:.3f}: {doc[:70]}...")
    
    # BM25 correctly ranks the exact error doc first
    # Dense might rank "process_list" first (semantically about lists)
```

**S9. 🧪 A/B test proving hybrid > BM25 alone.**

```python
from scipy import stats
import numpy as np

def ab_test_bm25_vs_hybrid(n_queries: int = 200) -> dict:
    """
    Simulate A/B test: BM25 alone vs BM25 + dense hybrid.
    """
    # Simulated NDCG@10 scores (based on typical BEIR findings)
    np.random.seed(42)
    
    # BM25: strong on exact-match, weak on semantic queries
    bm25_ndcg = np.concatenate([
        np.random.beta(6, 2, n_queries // 2) * 0.9,   # keyword queries: BM25 good
        np.random.beta(2, 4, n_queries // 2) * 0.8,   # semantic queries: BM25 poor
    ])
    
    # Hybrid: captures both keyword and semantic
    hybrid_ndcg = np.concatenate([
        np.random.beta(6, 2, n_queries // 2) * 0.92,  # keyword: roughly same
        np.random.beta(5, 2, n_queries // 2) * 0.85,  # semantic: hybrid wins
    ])
    hybrid_ndcg = np.clip(hybrid_ndcg, 0, 1)
    bm25_ndcg   = np.clip(bm25_ndcg, 0, 1)
    
    # Paired t-test
    t_stat, p_value = stats.ttest_rel(hybrid_ndcg, bm25_ndcg)
    diff = hybrid_ndcg - bm25_ndcg
    
    print("A/B Test: BM25 vs Hybrid")
    print(f"  BM25 NDCG@10:   {bm25_ndcg.mean():.4f} ± {bm25_ndcg.std():.4f}")
    print(f"  Hybrid NDCG@10: {hybrid_ndcg.mean():.4f} ± {hybrid_ndcg.std():.4f}")
    print(f"  Delta: {diff.mean():+.4f}")
    print(f"  t={t_stat:.3f}, p={p_value:.4f}")
    print(f"  Significant (α=0.05): {p_value < 0.05}")
    print(f"  Cohen's d: {diff.mean() / diff.std():.3f}")
    
    return {
        "bm25_mean": bm25_ndcg.mean(),
        "hybrid_mean": hybrid_ndcg.mean(),
        "delta": diff.mean(),
        "p_value": p_value,
        "significant": p_value < 0.05,
    }

ab_test_bm25_vs_hybrid()
```

```python
def recommend_search_architecture(requirements: dict) -> dict:
    """
    Architecture recommendation based on product requirements.
    
    Output: recommended stack + reasoning.
    """
    stack_options = {
        "BM25-only": {
            "stack": "Elasticsearch BM25",
            "conditions": [
                requirements.get("training_data", 0) < 5000,
                requirements.get("gpu_budget", False) == False,
                requirements.get("domain") in ["legal", "code", "ecommerce_sku"],
                requirements.get("latency_ms", 100) < 30,
            ],
        },
        "Dense-only": {
            "stack": "FAISS + sentence-transformers",
            "conditions": [
                requirements.get("training_data", 0) > 50_000,
                requirements.get("semantic_queries", 0) > 0.8,
                requirements.get("multilingual", False),
            ],
        },
        "BM25 + SPLADE": {
            "stack": "Elasticsearch + SPLADE encoder",
            "conditions": [
                requirements.get("training_data", 0) > 10_000,
                requirements.get("gpu_budget", False),
                requirements.get("latency_ms", 100) < 50,
            ],
        },
        "Hybrid (BM25 + Dense + CE)": {
            "stack": "Elasticsearch + FAISS bi-encoder + cross-encoder",
            "conditions": [
                requirements.get("quality_priority", False),
                requirements.get("training_data", 0) > 20_000,
                requirements.get("latency_ms", 100) >= 100,
            ],
        },
    }
    
    # Score each option
    scores = {}
    for name, option in stack_options.items():
        scores[name] = sum(int(c) for c in option["conditions"])
    
    winner = max(scores, key=scores.get)
    
    print("Architecture recommendation:")
    print(f"  Input requirements: {requirements}")
    print(f"  Scores: {scores}")
    print(f"  Recommended: {winner}")
    print(f"  Stack: {stack_options[winner]['stack']}")
    
    return {"recommendation": winner, "scores": scores}

# Example: startup with no training data, legal domain
recommend_search_architecture({

    "training_data": 2000,
    "gpu_budget": False,
    "latency_ms": 50,
    "semantic_queries": 0.3,
    "multilingual": False,
    "quality_priority": False,
})
```
